recipes.name: Hearty Meat Lasagna
ingredients_raw: 0.5 pound lean ground pork, veal or crumbled sausage
1 (455 ml) bottle Heinz® Chili Sauce, Chunky with Sweet Peppers

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (180 degrees C). Heat oil in a large saucepan or Dutch oven set over medium heat. Add onion, green pepper, garlic and dried herbs; cook for 5 to 10 minutes or until vegetables soften.

Crumble in beef and pork and brown all over, about 5 minutes. Stir in tomato juice, chili sauce, tomato paste and Worcestershire Sauce; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Spread 1/4 of the sauce in to a 13- x 9-in (3 L) casserole dish. Top with 3 noodles. Layer with 1/4 more sauce and 1/3 of the cheese. Repeat layers twice, ending with cheese.
Cover with foil and bake for 1 hour. Remove foil and bake for 15 minutes or until golden. Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Hearty Meat Lasagna
raw_recipe.description: This classic layered pasta, sauce and cheese dish gets a zesty boost with the addition of chunky, chili sauce.

review.reviewBody: I made this and everyone LOVED it. Thanks for sharing this recipe it was delicious.
I have a wonderful traditional recipe but thought I'd try this. There was a sweetness to the sauce that was unpleasant. I'll stick to the one I know and love.

It turned out really good. I used a store bought sauce to save a little time but also had to Doctor it up a bit more. This was my 1st time using sweet chili sauce in lasagna and it gave it a different flavor and I liked it. I also used the noodles that don't require boiling you just bake them...those I will never use again I didn't like them at all.

Will definitely use this recipe again.

I have made this lasagna before and really the recipe is very good. My only recommendation would be to buy medium moisture mozzarella cheese you will notice the difference in the end result. My actual tweak of this recipe lies in preparing bechamel sauce to add on top of the meat sauce on each layer. The difference that adding the aforementioned cheese can be noticed and if you add the bechamel it makes this recipe even better!
We were disappointed. The problem has to do with two things: the oven-ready lasagna and the lack of ricotta or other cheeses. The sauce is good, though!
